notes: Reconciled from coders A and B. No school or computing unit found in the collect file; course layer deferred. CCIT duplicate of the guidelines not coded. documents.unit: Division of Undergraduate Learning (Undergraduate Academic Processes Team)
documents.title: Guidance: Addressing Artificial Intelligence and Academic Integrity
documents.summary: October 2025 guidance from the Undergraduate Academic Processes Team to instructors on handling AI and academic integrity. It sets no AI rule itself, requires a syllabus AI policy, and offers preventative (clear expectations, assignment redesign) and reactive (evidence beyond detectors, conversation first) advice.
documents.stance_why: The document gives instructors advice and says 'your course AI policy is a required component of your syllabus'; it never sets a campus-wide AI rule for students, deferring to 'unauthorized AI use' as defined by each course, so delegates.

units.why: Says 'effective AI tutors' are 'very supportive of learning' in a class; framed as a tutoring use, so P12, informs and encouraging.
units.anchor: The development of effective AI tutors is one example of how this technology can be
units.resolution_why: Only B found it. Source: 'The development of effective AI tutors is one example of how this technology can be very supportive of learning within your class.' A real statement that AI tutoring supports learning, kept as P12 informs.

units.why: The guidance says "expectations placed on our students post-graduation suggest that the ethical and effective use of AI must now be an important college learning outcome"; it justifies teaching AI use as a professional skill, so P44 (the claim is about learning outcomes, informs).
units.anchor: the ethical and effective use of AI must now be an important college learning outcome
units.resolution_why: A coded actor all, B admin. The sentence 'the ethical and effective use of AI must now be an important college learning outcome' is a general principle stated to the whole university community, not a duty on administrators, so actor all. informs, P44 and encourage agreed.

units.why: Encourages faculty 'to visit a resource created by Clemson's Office of Institutional Effectiveness and our libraries' on positive classroom uses; faculty learning support, P63.

units.resolution_why: Only B found it. Source: 'we encourage you to visit a resource created by Clemson's Office of Institutional Effectiveness and our libraries'. A real pointer to faculty resources, kept as P63.

units.resolution_why: A coded actor all, B admin. 'these tools also challenge traditional definitions of academic originality and authorship' frames the scope and tension of the guidance for everyone; it binds no office, so actor all. P56 agreed.

units.why: Invites instructors: 'If you have found other approaches particularly valuable ... please reach out so that we can share them'; feedback invited, P54.

The bullet sits among 'Helpful tips for communicating your expectations' and says 'If you use AI for anything, sharing this example can further emphasize to students' the value of the tools: a recommendation to instructors, so should. It concerns the instructor's own AI use and sets no position on student use, so unit_stance neutral. P47 agreed.

documents.title: Generative AI Guidelines
documents.summary: University-wide generative AI guidelines mostly about data protection, approved tools, verification and transparency. For coursework it defers to the syllabus and instructor, and forbids submitting unauthorized AI-generated work as one's own.
documents.stance_why: The guidelines tell students to 'Follow your course syllabus/instructor rules on whether and how AI may be used', so the course-level decision is left to instructors. The university adds a data-protection layer and a default ban on unauthorized AI-generated graded work, but sets no single AI-use stance, so delegates.

units.why: Defines generative AI as 'systems that can create or transform content such as text, code, images, audio, video and summaries', setting the policy's subject; P61.
units.anchor: systems that can create or transform content such as text, code, images, audio, video and

units.why: Opening purpose statement: all community members are "responsible for protecting University information and complying with University policies" when using AI; a framework statement of purpose: P56.
units.anchor: responsible for protecting University information and complying with University policies, legal obligations and ethical standards
units.resolution_why: A coded P56 (framework), B coded P50 (data protection) for 'responsible for protecting University information and complying with University policies, legal obligations and ethical standards'. The sentence is in the Purpose section and covers policies, legal obligations and ethical standards, not only data, so it is the guidelines' framing duty, P56. The data-specific duties are coded separately as P50. Actor all, general, must agreed.

units.why: Says the guidelines give 'practical direction for using generative AI safely and responsibly', an institution-level framework statement; P56.
units.anchor: practical direction for using generative AI safely and responsibly
units.resolution_why: Only B found it (A's matching candidate was the preceding sentence). Source: 'These guidelines provide practical direction for using generative AI safely and responsibly'. It states what the guidelines are for, a purpose statement, so it is kept as P56 informs; actor all because it is addressed to the whole community rather than to administrators.

units.why: Places the guidelines in a hierarchy from university policy to department to course-specific requirements, "with more specific requirements taking precedence"; a framework of scope (P56). P04 not chosen because it does not say instructors decide AI permission.
units.anchor: more specific requirements taking precedence as applicable

units.why: Scope: guidelines 'apply to ... faculty, staff, students, contractors and affiliates when using generative AI tools for University work or coursework'; P61.
units.anchor: apply to Clemson University faculty, staff, students, contractors and affiliates

units.why: Core principle 'Use data classification to decide what can be entered into an AI system' is a data-protection rule; P50.
units.anchor: Use data classification to decide what can be entered into an AI system.

units.why: Core principle 'Prefer Clemson-approved services for University work', favoring vetted tools; P50.
units.anchor: Prefer Clemson-approved services for University work.

units.why: Core principle 'Assume outputs can be wrong. Verify AI-generated information using authoritative sources'; P31.
units.anchor: Verify AI-generated information using authoritative sources.

units.why: Principle "Be transparent": disclose and cite AI use "when required" by instructor or others; disclosure with a submission: P24.
units.anchor: Disclose and cite AI use when required by your instructor, publisher, sponsor
units.resolution_why: A coded unit_stance permit, B neutral. 'Disclose and cite AI use when required' is a disclosure condition on use that the guidelines treat as allowed, so permit, consistent with other P24 units.

units.why: Core principle 'You are accountable for decisions, work products and outcomes produced with AI assistance'; ownership of what is produced, P29.
units.anchor: You are accountable for decisions, work products and outcomes produced with AI assistance.
units.resolution_why: A coded phase general, B during-work. 'You are accountable for decisions, work products and outcomes produced with AI assistance' concerns the work done with AI, so during-work, as for other P29 units. Actor all, must, P29 agreed.

units.why: Defines 'Public AI tool (unapproved/public-facing)' as consumer services 'where Clemson has not approved the service for institutional data'; P61.
units.anchor: Consumer/public AI services where Clemson has not approved the service for institutional data.
units.resolution_why: Only B found it. Source: 'Consumer/public AI services where Clemson has not approved the service for institutional data.' It defines the public AI tool category used by the data rules, so it is kept as P61 informs.

units.why: Defines the category 'Clemson-approved, contract-protected AI service' as 'An AI service renewed and approved for University use' (e.g. ChatGPT Edu, Microsoft Copilot); definition that scopes the rules, P61.
units.anchor: An AI service renewed and approved for University use.
units.resolution_why: Only B found it. Source: 'An AI service renewed and approved for University use.' (definition of Clemson-approved, contract-protected AI service). It defines a tool category that the rules depend on, so it is kept as P61 informs.

units.why: Offers Microsoft Copilot and ChatGPT Edu as contract-protected enterprise tools; a sanctioned university AI tool, P17.
units.anchor: Examples: ChatGPT Edu, Microsoft Copilot
units.resolution_why: Only B found it. Source: 'Examples: ChatGPT Edu, Microsoft Copilot' as Clemson-approved AI services. It names the sanctioned tools, so it is kept as P17 informs.

units.why: Requires users to check the data and tool matrix before using any AI tool to see whether use is "permitted, requires prior approval, or is prohibited"; data protection and vetted tools: P50.
units.anchor: determine the applicable data classification and tool category, and consult this matrix
units.resolution_why: A coded P50, B coded P05 for 'Before using any AI tool, determine the applicable data classification and tool category, and consult this matrix to confirm whether the proposed use is permitted, requires prior approval, or is prohibited'. The sentence tells the reader to run a data-protection check before use. The matrix it points to is a table of data types by tool category, but the rule coded here is the duty to check, which belongs with data protection and vetted tools: P50. Actor all, before-course, must, restrict agreed.

units.why: Risk description: "prompts, uploads and outputs may be stored for a period of time"; data privacy fact: P50.

units.why: Warns 'Some services may use submitted content to improve models'; data-handling risk, P50.

units.resolution_why: Only B found it. Source: 'Some services may use submitted content to improve models.' A statement of a data-handling risk that supports the data rules, kept as P50 informs.

units.why: States AI 'can generate incorrect, fabricated or misleading content ("hallucinations"), including citations, calculations and code behavior'; P31.
units.anchor: AI tools can generate incorrect, fabricated or misleading content

units.why: Legal risk that outputs "may incorporate or resemble copyrighted or proprietary content": P52.
units.anchor: AI outputs may incorporate or resemble copyrighted or proprietary content.

units.why: Warns 'AI use may create plagiarism or authorship issues if not disclosed or permitted'; ties undisclosed use to plagiarism, P36.
units.anchor: AI use may create plagiarism or authorship issues if not disclosed or permitted.
units.resolution_why: A coded phase when-misuse, B general. 'AI use may create plagiarism or authorship issues if not disclosed or permitted' is a warning in the AI Risks section, not about suspicion or sanctions in a specific case, so general. informs, P36 agreed.

units.why: Warns 'Some uses can introduce bias, privacy harms or misuse of sensitive information'; P53.
units.anchor: Some uses can introduce bias, privacy harms or misuse of sensitive information.

units.why: Checklist step to 'Confirm whether the tools has contractual/administrative protections appropriate to the data'; vetted-tool and data rule, P50.

units.resolution_why: Only B found it. Source: 'Confirm whether the tools has contractual/administrative protections appropriate to the data'. A distinct checklist step, kept as P50 should.

units.anchor: If any of the information above is unclear: do not enter the data.
units.resolution_why: A coded phase before-course, B during-work. 'If any of the information above is unclear: do not enter the data' tells users what to do when they are about to enter data in an AI tool, which happens during the work, so during-work. must-not, P50 agreed.

units.why: Best practice: "Enter only public data into unapproved/public AI tools": P50.
units.anchor: Enter only public data into unapproved/public AI tools.

units.why: Best practice 'Minimize data. Share the least information necessary to accomplish the task'; P50.
units.anchor: Share the least information necessary to accomplish the task.
units.resolution_why: Only B found it. Source: 'Minimize data. Share the least information necessary to accomplish the task.' A distinct best practice, kept as P50 should.

units.why: Best practice banning pasting of passwords, tokens and keys into AI tools: P50.
units.anchor: Never paste secrets. Do not include passwords, access tokens, private keys
units.resolution_why: A coded unit_stance prohibit, B restrict. 'Never paste secrets. Do not include passwords, access tokens, private keys' is an outright ban on one kind of input, not a conditional limit, so prohibit. must-not, P50 agreed.

units.why: Best practice 'Treat AI outputs as untrusted. Verify facts, calculations, citations and claims'; P31.
units.anchor: Treat AI outputs as untrusted.
units.resolution_why: Only B found it. Source: 'Treat AI outputs as untrusted. Verify facts, calculations, citations and claims via authoritative sources.' This is in the Best Practices list, separate from the Core Principles statement, and is a real instruction, so it is kept as P31 should.

units.why: Best practice 'record the tool used, date and what was asked' for important use; documenting prompts, P26 (keep records) rather than P25 (which covers cite details in submissions).

units.resolution_why: A coded P25 (cite tool, prompt, output) with permit, B coded P26 (keep records) with neutral. 'record the tool used, date and what was asked' is a best practice for keeping a record of important use ('Document important use'), not the content of a citation in a submission, so P26. It sets no position on whether AI may be used, so neutral.

units.resolution_why: A coded instructor/should-not, B admin/informs. The sentence reports that Vanderbilt and Northwestern 'recommended they not be used as a basis for academic dishonesty allegations'. It is a peers' recommendation passed on to faculty, not an instruction from the Graduate School, so modality informs; the reader it is addressed to is the instructor. P39 agreed.

units.why: States 'Turnitin will flag Grammarly edited content as AI-generated', a limit on detection; P39.

documents.unit: Office of Teaching Effectiveness and Innovation
documents.title: AI Statements for Syllabi
tiers: AI Tools Permitted under NO Circumstances
AI Tools Permitted in Certain Circumstances
AI Tools Permitted for Course Work
AI Tools Integrated into the Course
documents.summary: Sample syllabus statements from the teaching center for four levels of AI use, from none to integrated. Faculty are told they need not follow them and the statements share documentation, understanding and integrity-process language.
documents.stance_why: The document offers four optional levels, 'varying from no use of AI to full use of AI', and says 'faculty are not required to follow these recommendations'; a template menu leaves the stance to each instructor, so delegates.

units.why: Describes 'four levels of AI use statements varying from no use of AI to full use of AI'; named levels, P05.
units.anchor: four levels of AI use statements varying from no use of AI to full use

units.why: States 'faculty are not required to follow these recommendations when creating their own AI syllabi statements'; the choice stays with each instructor, P04.
units.anchor: faculty are not required to follow these recommendations when creating their own AI syllabi statements.

units.why: Recommends syllabus statements give circumstances for AI use, a rationale and how violations are addressed; P09.
units.anchor: A description of the circumstances (if any) where AI tools may be used in the
units.policy: Syllabus AI statements describe the circumstances where AI tools may be used, give a rationale for the policy, and say how potential violations will be addressed.
units.resolution_why: A anchored the 'rationale' item and coded phase before-course; B anchored the 'description of the circumstances' item and coded course-start. Both are items in the list of what a syllabus statement should contain. The passage is about the content of expectations communicated to students in the syllabus, so course-start fits; actor instructor, modality should (suggested content, 'faculty are not required to follow'), type P09 agreed.

units.why: Tier 1 text bans AI "under any circumstances, even with proper documentation and citation": P01.
units.anchor: under any circumstances, even with proper documentation and citation
units.resolution_why: A coded during-work, B course-start. The passage 'not permitted for work in this course under any circumstances' bans AI use on course work, so the rule applies while students do the work: during-work. Course-start describes the act of communicating, which the other units on the statement already cover.

units.why: Level 1 rationale: skills 'are meant to come from your thinking and effort, not AI, in order to support your mastery of skills'; P41.
units.anchor: meant to come from your thinking and effort, not AI, in order to support your
units.resolution_why: A coded unit_stance prohibit, B neutral. The sentence only gives the reason for the ban ('meant to come from your thinking and effort, not AI'); the ban itself is a separate unit (P01). A rationale is neutral per the codebook.

units.why: 'Concerns regarding potential violations of this policy will be reviewed fairly through the appropriate university academic integrity process' (repeated in every level); P36.
units.anchor: will be reviewed fairly through the appropriate university academic integrity process

units.why: Level 2: 'You will be informed in writing as to when, where, and how these tools will be permitted'; per-assignment permission, P04.
units.anchor: You will be informed in writing as to when, where, and how these tools will
units.resolution_why: A coded student/informs, B instructor/must. The text, 'You will be informed in writing as to when, where, and how these tools will be permitted', is addressed to students but is an obligation on the instructor to communicate the permitted uses, so the actor it binds is the instructor and the modality must. P04 and course-start agreed.

units.why: Level 2: 'the ethical, responsible use of AI can support and enhance your learning'; rationale for permitting, P44 (nearest) as a learning benefit statement.
units.anchor: the ethical, responsible use of AI can support and enhance your learning
units.resolution_why: Only B found it. Source: 'I recognize ... the ethical, responsible use of AI can support and enhance your learning.' This is a real rationale statement for permitting AI in the 'certain circumstances' tier, so it is kept as P44 informs.

units.why: Where AI is allowed, use "must be documented and cited": P24.
units.anchor: Your responsible use of AI tools must be documented and cited
units.resolution_why: A coded unit_stance permit, B neutral. The documentation/citation requirement is a condition attached to permitted use ('Your responsible use of AI tools must be documented and cited'), so it sits within a permit stance, as for other disclosure units.

units.why: Level 2: 'you must be able to demonstrate understanding of the content of any work submitted'; P30.
units.anchor: you must be able to demonstrate understanding of the content of any work submitted
units.resolution_why: A coded unit_stance permit, B neutral. 'You must be able to demonstrate understanding' is an accountability duty rather than a position on whether AI may be used; neutral, as for other accountability units.

units.why: Level 2: 'Outside of these circumstances, AI tools should not be used for your work'; default ban when not specified, P06.
units.anchor: Outside of these circumstances, AI tools should not be used for your work.

units.why: Tier 3 says AI "is permitted for work in this course", a permissive default with conditions: P02.
units.anchor: The use of artificial intelligence (AI) tools is permitted for work in this course.
units.resolution_why: A coded during-work, B course-start. The sentence 'AI tools is permitted for work in this course' says what students may do while working, so during-work.

units.why: Level 3: 'you are accountable for the responsible, ethical use of these tools'; P29.
units.anchor: you are accountable for the responsible, ethical use of these tools
units.resolution_why: A coded unit_stance permit, B neutral. 'You are accountable for the responsible, ethical use' is an ownership/accountability duty (P29), not a position on AI use; neutral.

units.why: Level 4: 'The use of artificial intelligence (AI) tools is integrated into the work for this course'; AI built into the course, P02 (expected use).
units.anchor: The use of artificial intelligence (AI) tools is integrated into the work for this course.
units.resolution_why: A coded during-work/must, B course-start/informs. The sentence 'The use of AI tools is integrated into the work for this course' declares that AI is part of the work; it does not impose a duty on the student, so informs. It describes what happens during the work, so during-work. Type P02 and stance require agreed.

units.why: Tier 4 says outcomes "include developing your ability to use these tools effectively"; teaching AI use as a skill: P44.
units.anchor: learning outcomes include developing your ability to use these tools effectively
